ai.title: SDK version bump to 0.1.32
ai.summary: Bumped @codebuff/sdk to 0.1.32 in sdk/package.json. Updated publish-dry-run script to use bun run scripts/publish.ts instead of node scripts/publish.js. Internal maintenance only.

eli5.text: The assistant's tool kit was quietly updated to version 0.1.32, a routine behind-the-scenes refresh that bumps the version number and switches how the publishing check runs from the old tool to the new one. If you look, you'd see the version label change in the project file and the command used to prepare the kit now calls a different script. Nothing looks or behaves differently for anyone using the assistant today, it's the kind of tidy-up that keeps things running smoothly underneath.

ai.title: Stop truncating agent messages on server
ai.summary: Removed `getMessagesSubset` call in `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts`. Agent steps now use full `agentState.messageHistory` instead of token-limited subsets. Prevents context loss from server-side truncation.

eli5.text: You might notice that conversations with an agent no longer get cut off mid-way through. Previously, when an agent was working on something for you, the system would trim earlier parts of the conversation if it got too long, which sometimes caused it to forget important context. Now, the agent keeps the full history of your conversation in memory, so it stays on track even in longer interactions. This change only affects how the agent processes its own internal memory and doesn't require any action from you.

ai.title: Remove addsubgoal from TOOLSWHICHWONTFORCENEXTSTEP
ai.summary: Removed `add_subgoal` from `TOOLS_WHICH_WONT_FORCE_NEXT_STEP` in `common/src/tools/constants.ts`. This forces the agent to take a next step after adding a subgoal, preventing potential stalls. Internal change affecting agent loop behavior.

eli5.text: When the assistant adds a new sub-goal to your task list, it will now always continue working on your request instead of potentially getting stuck and stopping. Previously, adding a sub-goal was treated like a minor bookkeeping action that didn't require immediate follow-up, but that behavior could cause the assistant to pause in the middle of a multi-step task. This is a behind-the-scenes tweak to how the assistant's planning loop works, so you should notice smoother, uninterrupted progress when it breaks down complex requests into smaller steps.

ai.title: Fix relative path handling in SDK terminal command execution
ai.summary: SDK client now resolves relative paths for `run_terminal_command` using `path.resolve` against the session's working directory. Previously, `cwd` was passed directly, causing failures with relative paths. Updated `@codebuff/sdk` to version 0.1.33.

eli5.text: If you ask the assistant to run a terminal command using a path that isn't the full address (like just a folder name), it will now find the right place more reliably instead of possibly failing. This helps when commands depend on knowing which folder to start in. The fix is live today in the assistant's developer tools.

ai.title: unstablecache added to agents API route
ai.summary: The `GET` handler in `web/src/app/api/agents/route.ts` now uses Next.js `unstable_cache` to memoize the expensive agent aggregation query for 60 seconds, replacing the previous `force-dynamic` rendering. This change reduces database load by serving cached results with stale-while-revalidate semantics and explicit CDN headers. The cache key is `['agents-data']` with tag `['agents']`, and the response includes `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300`.

eli5.text: When someone views the list of agents, the page now shows a stored copy from the past minute instead of rebuilding it from scratch every single time, so the system doesn't have to do that heavy lookup over and over. If you refreshed the page, you might see agent metrics update up to a minute later than usual, and the system will quietly refresh the stored copy in the background. This only affects the internal agent listing route.

ai.title: Refactor agent store UI and CLI agent flag handling
ai.summary: CLI `--agent` flag now prefills input with `@agent` instead of direct invocation. Web agent detail page replaces separate `AgentUsageMetrics` card with inline `VersionUsageBadge` in version navigation. `RunAgentButton` and `SaveAgentButton` icons changed to `Play` and `Bookmark` respectively, with updated toast messages. `store/page.tsx` removes `isRecentlyUpdated` helper.

eli5.text: You know how when you want to run an agent from the command line, you'd type something directly? Now the tool quietly puts the agent's name into your input box first, so you can just press enter and edit it before running. In your web browser, when you look at an agent's details, the little usage numbers that used to sit in a separate box now appear right next to each version in the list, and the buttons for running and saving an agent have swapped their icons for a 'play' symbol and a bookmark, with clearer messages that pop up after you click. None of this changes what the agents can actually do, it's all about making the screens and commands look and feel cleaner.

ai.title: run-eval-set default agent base-lite
ai.summary: evals/git-evals/run-eval-set.ts changed `agent` flag default from `base` to `base-lite`. Affects default agent selection for eval runs. No migration needed.

eli5.text: When running automated test batches that compare different versions of our AI assistant, the system now uses a faster, simpler assistant mode by default instead of the standard one. If you manage or schedule these test runs, you will get quicker results without any extra setup, though you can still switch back to the standard mode if needed.

ai.title: await SDK custom tool handler result
ai.summary: SDK client now awaits custom tool handler results in sdk/src/client.ts. Ensures async handler completion before returning. Scope limited to SDK client. Imported PublishedClientToolName as type-only.

eli5.text: When the assistant uses a custom tool you've programmed, the SDK client now waits for that tool to finish running before moving on. Previously, it could return the result while the tool was still working behind the scenes, leaving you with incomplete or inconsistent data. This only affects the SDK client, and you'd notice that custom tool results are now fully completed and reliable every time.

ai.title: SDK custom tool handler renamed to execute
ai.summary: The `handler` property in `CustomToolDefinition` is renamed to `execute` to align with the ai-sdk standard. Type parameters `Args` and `Input` default to `unknown` instead of `any`. This change affects `sdk/src/custom-tool.ts` and `sdk/src/client.ts`, requiring updates to any custom tool definitions using the old property name.

eli5.text: When someone writes a custom tool that plugs into the assistant, they used to give the tool's action a property called 'handler'; now they must call it 'execute'. The tool system also stopped accepting completely unknown input types by default, making custom tools a bit stricter about what data they accept. If you build these kinds of tools, your existing definitions will need their property renamed; otherwise, nothing you see day to day changes.

ai.title: Support sync handlers in custom-tool execute
ai.summary: The `execute` handler in `getCustomToolDefinition` now accepts synchronous return values alongside promises. The SDK internally wraps the user-provided function in an async closure to ensure consistent handling. This change is reflected in the `sdk/src/custom-tool.ts` file and version bump to `0.2.0`.

eli5.text: Custom tools in the SDK can now use simpler, synchronous functions instead of only promise-based ones. When a developer builds a custom tool, their function can return its result directly rather than wrapping it in a promise. You wouldn't notice anything different unless you create these tools yourself, but the SDK now handles both styles smoothly by wrapping every call in an async routine behind the scenes. This is already live as part of the 0.2.0 release.
